Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — confirmation and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap of the PII/data controls we discussed and the concrete confirmations you asked for. I pulled together the short answers below and attached a one-page summary + SOC2 stub and a simple data flow diagram for your procurement team.

Key confirmations (short):
- What we store: by default, Redwood logs request metadata (timestamp, model, route, token counts) and request/response text for hosted API customers to support quality monitoring, safety, and billing. For prompts/outputs specifically: we DO persist the raw prompt and model output for the retention window unless a customer opts into one of the opt-out options below.
- Retention duration: default retention is 30 days for hosted accounts. We offer configurable retention policies for Dedicated and Private customers (can be shortened to 0 days/disabled). For enterprise contracts we can set custom retention (e.g., 0/7/30/90 days) in the agreement.
- Logging controls: customers can request
  - Prompt/output logging disabled (no raw text stored)
  - Only metadata + token counts retained
  - Redaction rules applied at the ingestion layer (regex-based, configurable)
  These controls are available via account settings for Dedicated/Private, and via an enterprise config for hosted production tenants.
- Data residency: we can pin storage and processing to US or EU regions for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For strict residency needs we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed VPC.
- Access and encryption: all stored artifacts are encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit; access is role-based and logged. We provide audit logs on request and can integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments.
- How outputs are used: stored prompts/outputs are used for debugging, quality/regression monitoring, and safety evaluations. We do NOT use customer data to train or improve public models unless agreed in writing.

Attachments included: redwood_pii_handling_summary.pdf, SOC2-type2-2025-stub.pdf, data_flow_diagram.png

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want logging disabled for the pilot, reply with "disable-hosted-logging" and we'll issue a config change for your tenant.
2) If you need a written statement for procurement, we'll provide a short notice confirming retention/residency settings once you pick the desired retention option (0/7/30/90).
3) Schedule a 30-min security Q&A with our security engineer (Marissa) if you want to go deeper on audit logs/KMS.

Let me know which option you prefer and I’ll get Rishi to prepare the contract language.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from procurement/security before we escalate to legal: 

1) When you say default 30 days, is that an absolute deletion after 30 days (i.e., zero retrievable copies), or is it just removed from the product console but retained in backups for X more days? We need explicit language that deleted data is not used for model training and that backups are handled per your backup/retention policy.

2) For the "disable-hosted-logging" option — are there any feature limitations when logging is disabled (e.g., no streaming/tracing, limited debugging)?

3) Does the SOC2 stub you attached include the control mapping for data retention and encryption? Procurements wants to see the table mapping controls to evidence.

Also, Daniel flagged that for pilot we want hosted but with logging disabled and US-only residency. Can you confirm that's possible and what we need to sign/acknowledge?

Thanks — Priya

Hi Priya — answering inline and confirming specifics for your procurement/security teams.

1) Backups and true deletion: for hosted tenants we retain backups for disaster recovery for a standard SLA window (up to 90 days) but backups are encrypted and access is tightly controlled; we can provide a deletion certification for retention=0 contracts. Importantly, we WILL NOT use customer data for model training or improve public models absent written consent. I attached the SOC2 evidence index which maps the retention and encryption controls — see the "Retention & Backup" section on page 2 of the stub.

2) Feature limitations when logging disabled: disabling prompt/output logging removes stored raw text from our logs and any features that rely on stored transcripts. Streaming generation (token streaming) and the API remain functional; however:
  - You will lose end-to-end transcript history in the Console UI.
  - Some debugging features (per-request replay in the Console) will be unavailable.
  - Metrics/quality alerts that require stored outputs will be degraded.
These limitations are usually acceptable for pilots; Marissa can walk through which observability UI pieces are impacted.

3) SOC2 mapping: the attached SOC2-type2-2025-stub includes a control mapping table for encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and retention. For full attestations we can coordinate a vendor questionnaire and produce supplemental extracts.

Pilot configuration confirmation:
- Hosted tenant with logging disabled and US-only residency: possible. Action items for us:
  1) You send a written confirmation to enable "disable-hosted-logging" for your tenant (we'll reply with a signed change order).
  2) We will set storage/residency to the US region for the tenant and confirm by providing a new data residency statement.
  3) Rishi will prepare contract language that includes the 30/90/0 retention SLA options and an explicit non-training clause (no use of customer content for model training without written consent).

Rishi — can you prepare the change order + contract language and the short procurement-ready statement? Marissa — can you take point on a 30-min walkthrough of the Console limitations for disabled logging?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
